topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Prerequisites: Visualizing Planarity
lecture_lines: Planar graphs draw in 2D with no edges crossing.
A 'face' is any enclosed region, including the exterior.
Visualize a house: five vertices, six edges.
The house has two interior and one exterior face.
Three faces total: satisfy the planarity condition.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Connected planar graphs follow Euler’s Characteristic formula.
Vertices minus edges plus faces equals two.
$V - E + F = 2$ acts as a structural invariant.
Flatten a cube to see this in action.
Eight vertices, twelve edges, six faces, totals two.

sections.title: The Concept of Dual Graphs
lecture_lines: Dual graphs simplify complex graph structures.
Place a vertex in every graph face.
Connect vertices if original faces share an edge.
animations: Place a dot in the center of each face of a planar graph [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Draw edges between dots corresponding to adjacent graph faces.
Highlight the dual graph in dashed lines #FFFFFF [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

sections.title: Interplay: Duality and Euler
lecture_lines: Dual of a dual graph returns the original.
Duality maps original vertices to dual faces.
Duality maps original faces to dual vertices.
Edge count remains the same in duality.
Euler’s characteristic stays constant through duality.
animations: Show original graph and its dual graph side-by-side using grid cells [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg].
Highlight correspondence between V of dual and F of original.
Animate the transformation satisfying the Euler formula.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Planar graphs are vital for circuit design.
Euler’s formula verifies layout efficiency.
Topology reveals deep geometric invariants.
